actions.title: Extract the categories, stats, error-log, consent, app-lock and factory-reset handlers into their own routes/*.ts files following the registerXRoutes pattern already used for accounts, transactions, rules, imports, analytics, backups and plaid, and move the fs/crypto imports to the top of server.ts.
Pass an AbortSignal.timeout(...) on each of the four relay calls in relay.ts so a hung relay fails fast rather than stalling the caller.
REDACTED: a MED severity finding in the security lens is withheld from the public copy. See this project's own bar-raise report for detail.
Replace the per-merchant loop in merchantTrendsBulk with one query filtered by `normalized_merchant IN (...)` and the shared date window, then bucket the rows per merchant in memory.

Add a bulk-uncategorize endpoint (or relax bulk-categorize to accept a null categoryId) that resolves the whole id list inside one db.transaction(), the same pattern bulk-categorize already uses, and point uncategorizeSelected at it instead of the per-row Promise.all.
Add a step to preship.ps1, or a CI job with PowerShell available, that runs scripts\audit-findings.selftest.ps1 and fails the gate on any fixture mismatch.
Call logEvent from the three catch blocks in runDailyMaintenance (server.ts), or push the logging into backup.ts itself so pruneIfDue and snapshotIfDue record their own failures.

Anchor resolveDateMMDD to a fixed reference (a required statement date field, or the first-import date recorded for that pasted text) instead of the live clock, and add a test that pins the resolved year for the same input text across two simulated system times straddling the flip point.

Add a test that runs a real import, calls rollbackImport on its batch id, and asserts the batch's transactions and import_errors are gone, a sibling batch's rows survive, and the imports row reads status='rolled_back'.

Either run scripts/post-audit-digests.ps1 standalone (it already supports that per scripts/README.md's Standalone use section) on a schedule independent of release.ps1, or catch the release-cadence gap itself so the next real release picks up both pending files within the existing cap of 5.
Sweep any imports row still 'pending' at boot into a 'failed' or 'interrupted' status, matching the pattern already used for the in-process throw case.
Add a rule identifier column written at categorize time, then a filter or a tile listing rows whose recorded rule no longer matches the rule now active for that category.
Resolve the visibility once (public vs private) and correct whichever of docs/privacy.md and docs/LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md is wrong, so the auditable-source promise matches the repository's actual state.

Write a small publish script (or a preship/release step) that copies docs/landing-page.html verbatim into the YaE repo path and fails loudly on a diff, or delete the in-repo template in favor of one canonical source, so the two copies cannot drift unnoticed.
